Findings.Comment: Using `!=` compares the two boxed `Long` object references, not their numeric account ids. When the persisted source account id and the requester id are equal values represented by different `Long` instances, which is common for ids outside the JVM cache range, the rightful source account is rejected with `TransferAccessDeniedException` and cannot cancel its own pending transfer.
Findings.Headline: Compare account ids by value when authorizing cancellation

Expected.why: Boxed Longs are compared by reference, so for any account id above 127 the owner's own cancellation is rejected as access denied.
The response body is never closed on any path, so the underlying connection is leaked on every call, successful or not.

Findings.Comment: `worker` now reads `q.pending` and writes `q.depth` without holding `q.mu`, while `Submit` can concurrently append to `q.pending` and `Depth` reads `q.depth` under the mutex. A submit arriving just as a job finishes creates a Go data race on the slice header and depth field, and can report a stale or inconsistent backlog.
Findings.Headline: Restore locking around worker depth update

Expected.why: The worker goroutine writes q.depth and reads q.pending without holding q.mu, while Submit writes and Depth reads the same fields under the mutex; that is a data race.

Findings.Comment: When `Disable` is called with an unknown slug, it returns before reaching the new unlock, leaving `r.mu` locked. The next registry operation that needs this mutex blocks forever, so a single bad slug can deadlock the registry.
Findings.Headline: Unlock mutex on the unknown-team path

Expected.why: The Unlock now runs only on the success path, so returning the unknown-team error leaves r.mu locked and every subsequent caller blocks forever.

Findings.Comment: The retry predicate is inverted: for a 500 or 429 response `post` returns a transient error, `retryable(lastErr)` is true, and `Deliver` returns on the first attempt instead of backing off. For a permanent 4xx it falls through and retries up to `maxAttempts`, contradicting the documented behavior.
Findings.Headline: Transient failures return immediately instead of retrying

Expected.why: Transient failures such as a 503 are now returned on the first attempt without any retry, while permanently rejected deliveries are retried five times with backoff.
